newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian retail coffee prices seen on rising trend.
newsitem.headline: Indian retail coffee prices seen on rising trend.

text.p: India's retail coffee prices are rising after a dip in output and gains by world prices, exporters and planters said on Monday.

"Coffee powder prices rose by 10 rupees per kg on February 23 and by another 10 rupees on Monday. It is expected to rise by another 10 rupees before March-end," said A.P. Jayakumar, secretary of the All India Coffee Merchants Association (AICMA).
"That will make the price 180 rupees per kg," Jayakumar said.
AICMA sets the retail price for soluble coffee.
Traders said soluble coffee was priced at 160 rupees a year ago. Prices touched a peak of 180 in 1995 following frosts in Brazil.
AICMA president R.P. Sarathy said arabica coffee was in short supply.

"Of the 80,000 tonnes (of arabica) expected to be produced this year, 47,500 tonnes have already been contracted for exports by exporters and growers," he said. "By June-July there will be a severe crunch."
Growers are keen to export and take advantage of a favourable global market.
The U. S. State Department has estimated world coffee production in 1996/97 (Oct-Sept) at 97 million bags of 60 kg each, against consumption of 99 million.
"This will keep the world prices high in the coming months. Exporters have already contracted till May," said Appaya a planter.
Sarathy said domestic traders lacked stocks and growers were selling to them at high prices. "So we are left with no option but to raise the prices in the retail market."
Planters said a fall in output had contributed to the shortage in the domestic market.
Planters and officials differed on coffee output in 1996/97.
"The output in 1996/97 season will not exceed 190,000 tonnes," said I.J.J. Rebello, chairman of the coffee committee of the United Planters Association of Southern India (UPASI).
Jayakumar said the crop would be only around 180,000 tonnes.
An official of the state-run Coffee Board said, "We will have a crop of around 205,000 tonnes comprising 89,950 tonnes of arabica and 115,000 tonnes of robusta."
In May the board estimated 1996/97 output at 219,000 tonnes but scaled it down to 205,000 in November.
India produced 200,000 tonnes of coffee in 1995/96, comprising 95,000 tonnes of arabica and 105,000 of robusta.
